title: pkg/machine/hyperv: detach 9p server from parent console
body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Podman!
-->

### Description

On Windows, when starting a Hyper-V machine in CMD.EXE or PowerShell, the background 9p server (`podman.exe machine server9p`) was started without detached process creation flags. Because `podman.exe` is a console subsystem application, Windows automatically attached it to the caller's console session. Closing the CMD.EXE/PowerShell window sent a console close event and terminated the 9p server process, causing 9p volume mounts (such as `/etc/containers`) in the VM to fail with input/output errors.

This change:
1. Configures `SysProcAttr` with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` on the 9p server command so it runs detached from the terminal session.
2. Decouples standard handles by redirecting `Stdin`, `Stdout`, and `Stderr` to `os.DevNull` (when debug file logging is not enabled) to prevent terminal sessions from hanging on exit due to open console handles.

Fixes: #29573

@Luap99 I've updated the PR and removed the redundant `devNull` block as suggested.

@l0rd @lstocchi When you have a moment, could you please take a look and test/confirm on Windows? Thank you!
@prabhat-kumar96 I have tested your fix, but the `podman machine server9p` process gets killed anyway. Have you tested on your side? If so, can you share the commands you used so I can try them too?

@l0rd updated the PR!

- `server9p` now uses `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (same as the WSL commands in `wutil.go`)
- added `DETACHED_PROCESS` for `gvproxy` and `win-sshproxy`

For `winmake.ps1` — checked it and it already pulls `gvproxy-windows-arm64.exe` for arm64, so that one should be fine.

To test on Hyper-V (as admin):
```powershell
.\winmake.ps1 podman-remote && .\winmake.ps1 win-gvproxy
$env:CONTAINERS_HELPER_BINARY_DIR = "$pwd\bin\windows"
$env:CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER = "hyperv"
.\winmake.ps1 localmachine "start_test.go"
```

To manually reproduce the original issue, start a machine, close the terminal, open a new one, and run podman ps / podman machine ssh -- "cat /etc/containers/storage.conf" — should work fine now.

> For winmake.ps1 — checked it and it already pulls gvproxy-windows-arm64.exe for arm64, so that one should be fine.

I made a mistake in my comment, but:

`gvproxy-windows-arm64.exe`  ==> **Console application** that we currently download
`gvproxy-arm64.exe`  ==> **GUI application** that we should download instead

Anyway, you don't need to make the change in this PR (using the DETACH_PROCESS flag solves the problem with the console version of gvproxy too). I can open a separate PR for this.
I have opened a [separate PR to fix the gvproxy version pulled on arm64](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29686).
